text.p: Mattel Inc., the nation's biggest toymaker, said Friday it amended its $755 million merger agreement with Tyco Toys Inc. to reflect a change in the conversion of Tyco shares.

Mattel spokesman Glenn Bozarth said the amendment calls for holders of Tyco Class C shares to receive preferred Mattel shares. Under the agreement announced Monday, Class C shareholders were to receive Mattel common stock valued at $12.50.
Common shares of Tyco edged down 12.5 cents to $11.50, while Mattel fell 37.5 cents to $30.125, both on the New York Stock Exchange.
Bozarth said the decision to amend the agreement came after holders of the Class C shares expressed concern.
"We were aware of the issue," he said.
The proposed union will combine Mattel's Barbie dolls, Hot Wheels miniature cars and Fisher-Price toys with Tyco's Matchbox cars, Sesame Street toys and radio-controlled vehicles.
Tyco, based in Mount Laurel, N.J., is the nation's third-largest toymaker, with 1995 revenues of $709 million. Mattel, based in El Segundo, Calif., had 1995 sales of $3.6 billion.
